attempt_1.experiment: Tried adding 5 real-world Tomato__Target_Spot images (cropped from UF/IFAS EDIS PP351, (c) University of Florida) to the stage2_tomato fine-tuning set, since PlantDoc has zero images for this class anywhere.
attempt_1.outcome: NOT PROMOTED -- did not help, and cost a small amount of accuracy elsewhere.

target_spot_heldout_check.description: 2 Target_Spot images never used in training, checked directly after fine-tuning (PlantDoc's test split has zero Target_Spot images, so this was the only real check available).
target_spot_heldout_check.result: 0/2 correct -- ts_leaves_topleft.jpg predicted Tomato_Bacterial_spot (conf 0.31), ts_ring_lesion.jpg predicted Tomato_Early_blight (conf 0.82). n=2 is not a statistically meaningful number; it's a sanity check, and it failed.

collateral_effect.description: Adding the 5th class's gradient signal to the shared stage2_tomato softmax head shifted predictions on the classes that COULD be measured.

attempt_1.conclusion: 5 images is not enough real-world signal to teach a 10-way softmax classifier a new class, and trying anyway measurably hurt the classes that already had real data.

attempt_2.experiment: Sourced 15 more real-world Target_Spot photos (20 total with attempt 1's images) from a second source: the CC BY 4.0 'Tomato Leaf Dataset' (Imtiaz et al., American International University Bangladesh, Mendeley Data DOI 10.17632/bpfd9cns5g.2) -- real field photos from tomato gardens in Bangladesh. That dataset ships YOLO bounding-box labels with no class-name file; class index 0 was identified as Target_Spot by downloading its labeled images and visually confirming the characteristic concentric-ring lesion against the UF/IFAS reference photos (18 of 20 class-0-labeled images showed a clearly visible lesion on inspection; 2, IMG_0303/IMG_0304, showed no visible symptom in frame and were excluded).
attempt_2.outcome: PROMOTED -- a human judgment call (see conversation), not a clean win. Real progress, still unreliable.

target_spot_heldout_check.description: 5 Target_Spot images never used in training (2 UF/IFAS + 3 Mendeley), checked directly after fine-tuning.
target_spot_heldout_check.result: 1/5 correct -- IMG_0349.jpg correctly predicted Tomato__Target_Spot (conf 0.85). The other 4 (ts_leaves_topleft.jpg, ts_ring_lesion.jpg, IMG_0653.jpg, IMG_1128.jpg) were misclassified as Bacterial_spot, Early_blight, Leaf_Mold, and Septoria_leaf_spot respectively. n=5 is still a small sample; this is a sanity check, not a benchmark.

collateral_effect.description: Same shared-softmax-head effect as attempt 1, smaller this time.

attempt_2.conclusion: 20 real images moved Target_Spot from 'always wrong' (0/2) to 'right 1 time in 5' (1/5), at a smaller collateral cost (-1.2pp vs attempt 1's -2.35pp) than before. Promoted on the user's explicit call that some real ability beats none, but this is NOT a fix -- it is still wrong on the large majority of real Target_Spot photos. A more reliable result would need substantially more real data still (the other 9 tomato classes have 44-140 real images each; Target_Spot has 20).

active_checkpoint: attempt_2's checkpoints are the currently active checkpoints/*_best.pt. Rollback path: *_plantdoc_no_target_spot.pt (pre-attempt-1 PlantDoc fine-tune) -> *_plantvillage_only.pt (original, no real-world fine-tuning at all).
